name: Manjunath Adinavar
valueChainDetail: Agricultural on-farm services — precision drone spraying for sunflower, maize, soybean, onion, paddy and arecanut.
profile:
Manjunath Adinavar, 35, is a farmer and a member of the Ranebennur Farmers Producer Company. He cultivates a diverse range of crops, including sunflower, maize, soybean, onion, and paddy.
He is also actively involved in drone-based agricultural livelihood activities, particularly in providing drone-based farm services.
whyChampion:
Manjunath Adinavar is a progressive farmer and agricultural technology champion from Ranebennur, with a network of 1,000+ farmers.
He actively promotes precision spraying and drone-based agricultural services, creating awareness and encouraging local farmers to adopt these technologies.
As a DGCA-approved drone pilot, he also provides drone repair, maintenance, and troubleshooting support to surrounding drone users. In addition, he has practical knowledge of tractors, weeders, power tillers, and other farm machinery, and promotes their adoption in the local area.
His technical expertise, farmer network, and hands-on support make him a strong local resource person and champion for agricultural mechanization and precision farming.
achievement:
Manjunath has covered more than 1,430 acres through drone-based spraying, generating revenue of approximately ₹7.5 lakh. He has conducted drone demonstrations and awareness programmes, promoting precision spraying across crops such as arecanut, sunflower, soybean, and others, and has supported 100+ farmers in adopting drone-based spraying.
In addition, he promotes agricultural mechanization in remote and underserved areas, helping farmers access modern technologies to improve farm efficiency and productivity.
successStory:
Manjunath has covered more than 1,430 acres through drone-based spraying, generating a total revenue of approximately ₹7.5 lakh. This additional income has strengthened his family’s financial position, improved income stability, and enhanced livelihood security.
Before the intervention, he cultivated only 1 acre of soybean, maize and other crops, generating limited and uncertain income. Through SELCO’s intervention, he was supported to establish a drone-based agricultural spraying service — earning ₹7.15 lakh in gross service revenue against an operating cost of approximately ₹1.43 lakh, a net operating income of ₹5.72 lakh/year (₹47,667/month).
The drone-based service has created a reliable alternative income stream, reducing dependence on farming alone and providing greater financial resilience for his family.
uniqueness:
Manjunath’s site serves as a local agricultural technology demonstration and service hub, combining drone-based precision spraying, farm machinery promotion, technical support, and farmer training.
With a network of 1,000+ farmers, 100+ drone-adopting farmers, and DGCA-approved piloting and repair skills, he acts as a local resource person and technology champion, enabling farmers in remote areas to access, understand, and adopt modern agricultural technologies.
selcoEngagement:
Through the geography team, end users were identified (young, who understand digital technologies, with a good network of farmers).
Support provided: financial gap support for the drone, DGCA training, and training on drone repair.

name: Ramesh Khangoudra
organisation: Resource person — NMNF, organic farming & mechanization programmes, Belagavi
tagline: Solar oil mill, turmeric & farm mechanization hub
valueChainDetail: Sugarcane, turmeric, oilseeds (groundnut, safflower) and dairy — farm-to-value-addition.
implementation: 2021–22: Solar-powered oil mill · 2023: Multipurpose toolbar · 2024: Oil filtration & filling system and oil-cake powdering unit
profile:
Ramesh Khangoudra is a 42-year-old diversified farmer from Kalloli, Belagavi, managing 10 acres of land under cultivation. He grows sugarcane, turmeric, onion, and maize, while supplementing his income through dairy, poultry, and small-scale oil extraction.
He uses a multipurpose toolbar for various on-farm activities, improving farm-level mechanization and operational efficiency.
whyChampion:
Integrated livelihood model: combines diversified farming with turmeric and oilseed value addition, dairy, poultry, and mechanized farm activities, creating multiple income streams.
Adopter of new technologies who shares feedback: demonstrates and promotes solar-powered oil milling, turmeric pulverization, oil filtration/filling, oil-cake processing, and multipurpose farm mechanization.
Strong farmer outreach and training: his farm serves as a demonstration and learning centre, receiving around 500 farmers monthly and training nearly 100 farmers each month on natural and organic farming.
Local resource person for multiple agriculture programmes in Belagavi, including natural farming (NMNF), organic farming, mechanization, and value-addition programmes.
achievement:
Ramesh’s farm has evolved into a local demonstration and learning centre, attracting around 500 farmers every month for exposure visits focused on value addition and farm-based technologies.
He regularly trains farmers in natural and organic farming practices, with approximately 100 farmers receiving training each month, helping strengthen local knowledge, technology adoption, and sustainable farming practices.
successStory:
Ramesh has transformed his livelihood from being primarily dependent on cultivation and dairy into a diversified farm-to-value-addition enterprise. With a solar-powered oil mill, turmeric pulverizer, multipurpose toolbar, oil filtration and filling system, and oil-cake powdering unit, he now undertakes value addition of groundnut, safflower, turmeric and other farm produce.
Today, his allied activities generate approximately ₹2–3 lakh per month apart from cultivation, strengthening household income security. Many oil mills and related technologies have been adopted in North Karnataka after exposure visits to his site.
uniqueness:
Ramesh’s site is unique as an integrated farm-to-enterprise demonstration hub, combining natural farming, mechanization, solar-powered processing, turmeric and oilseed value addition, and farmer training.
With 500+ farmers visiting monthly and 100+ farmers trained, the site demonstrates how technology, value addition, and knowledge sharing can create a replicable and diversified rural livelihood model.
selcoEngagement:
SELCO identified Ramesh as a progressive organic farmer through the geography team and, based on the livelihood assessment, supported the introduction of appropriate technologies for farm mechanization and value addition.
SELCO’s engagement has evolved beyond technology deployment to demonstration, capacity building, and farmer outreach. He conducts an average of 5 exposure visits per month and provides need-based training to farmers and institutions from different parts of Karnataka.

name: Irappa Barekar
occupation: Farmer & Founder – Ayur Swasth Agro Products
organisation: Ayur Swasth Agro Products · NMNF training centre
address: Madli Village, Post: Dundashi, Taluk: Shiggaon, District: Haveri, Karnataka – 581193
valueChainDetail: Millets (ragi, little millet, foxtail), pulses (tur dal, pigeon pea), oilseeds and vegetables → processing → SHG value addition → branded products.
implementation: 2025 — Millet Processing Unit and Dal Processing Unit
profile:
Irappa Barekar, 33, is a young farmer and agri-processing entrepreneur (ITI) from Madli Village, Shiggaon, Haveri. He owns 2.5 acres and cultivates ragi, little millet, navane and vegetables.
He has developed an integrated farm-to-processing enterprise with a millet processing unit, dal mill, oil extraction unit, cold-press grinding machine and dairy farm. His value-added products include millet flour and mixes, groundnut oil, safflower oil, ghee, wheat flour, and jowar flour — sold under the brand Ayur Swasth.
whyChampion:
Irappa is an active farmer and value-addition entrepreneur managing multiple agricultural and processing activities. His existing millet, oil extraction, dal processing and dairy facilities make the site suitable as a demonstration and learning site for millet growing, processing and value addition.
He has a network of about 500 farmers in surrounding areas, good knowledge of millet cultivation and processing, and acts as a resource person for the training of other farmers.
achievement:
Selected as a training centre under the National Mission on Natural Farming (NMNF) for value addition and natural farming training (250 members under the programme).
More than 100 farmers visit the site every month and more than 500 farmers have been trained so far. He established Ayur Swasth Agro Products with three young farmers and trains 40–50 farmers every month on cultivation, expense and profit management, and marketing.
successStory:
A young farmer who left his job to return to agriculture, Irappa has diversified from primary cultivation into value-added products — millet flours, millet mixes, groundnut oil, safflower oil, ghee, wheat flour and jowar flour.
Earlier he relied on external facilities for millet and dal processing. After SELCO’s intervention he processes his own millets and procures pulses from FPOs and other farmers for dal processing and sale, transforming the unit into a diversified millet and dal processing enterprise. More than 50 farmers have expanded land under millets because he buys raw material locally.
uniqueness:
The site is located within the farm, where millets, vegetables, and other crops are cultivated organically. The farm also integrates dairy and goat rearing with primary processing and value addition, creating a diversified, integrated farming enterprise.
It can train up to 100 farmers in a batch and is a learning centre for cultivation, primary processing and value addition.
selcoEngagement:
In collaboration with the agriculture department, the progressive farmer was identified; after assessment SELCO Foundation supported the Millet Processing Unit and the Dal Mill Processing Unit (co-created based on his problem statement).
The Millet Mentor programme supported machinery procurement, technical training, market linkages and solar infrastructure on a soft repayment plan. More than 10 exposure visits and about 5 trainings on millet cultivation and processing have been conducted at this site.

name: R. Lohith
tagline: Arecanut husk to vermicompost — circular farming
address: K. Ganadakatte, Channagiri Taluk, Davanagere District, Karnataka
valueChainDetail: Arecanut waste → drying → shredding → husk powder → vermicompost / mushroom substrate / growing medium.
implementation: Arecanut husk shredder + solar drying + vermicomposting guidance
profile:
R. Lohith is a graduate farmer from K. Ganadakatte, Channagiri, engaged in agriculture, mushroom cultivation and organic input preparation, including home-based vermicomposting using processed arecanut husk. He supports a family of 14.
Annual income: ~₹15 lakh from agriculture crops and ₹7–9 lakh from mushrooms.
whyChampion:
Lohith is a Champion End User for his practical adoption of an integrated climate-smart package of practices that converts arecanut husk waste into a useful organic input in the circular economy.
His model combines waste management, vermicomposting, sustainable farming and livelihood diversification, with potential for replication in other arecanut-growing regions.
achievement:
State-Level Progressive Farmer Award – honoured by the Chief Minister of Karnataka (presented by VK Newspaper).
Best Agri-Entrepreneur Award – Keladi Shivappa Nayaka University of Agricultural and Horticultural Sciences, Shivamogga.
State-Level Raita Ratna Award.
DAESI Gold Medalist & Best Student (National Level) – MANAGE, Hyderabad.
successStory:
Earlier, arecanut husk was bulky, piled up as waste and took up to 2 years to decompose, with limited value-addition options. With the shredder and solar drying solution, he now processes the husk and uses it as a resource for vermicomposting and other applications.
Husk decomposition dropped from ~2 years to a few weeks, drying time fell from 60 days to 3 days with the solar dryer, and waste utilisation went from minimal to full. Mushroom substrate and areca-peat applications are now under trial.
uniqueness: A working circular-economy site where arecanut husk — usually dumped by the roadside — becomes powder for vermicompost, mushroom substrate and growing media. Shredder capacity is 15–20 kg dry husk per hour, and 100 kg of wet husk yields ~15 kg of powder.
selcoEngagement:
SELCO Foundation identified Lohith through field engagement in arecanut-growing regions where biomass waste management is a persistent challenge. His interest in mushroom cultivation and organic farming made him an early adopter.
Support: arecanut husk shredder, solar drying approach, and technology and knowledge support for husk processing and vermicomposting.

name: Raghu R. S.
organisation: CEO, Shree Arogya Food and Beverages Products (Brand: Tapasvi)
tagline: Millet cookies under the Tapasvi brand
valueChainDetail: Farmers/FPOs → millet grains → processing → millet cookies → consumers / institutional buyers.
implementation: Solar infrastructure via the Millet Mentor programme
profile:
Raghu R. S. is the CEO of Shree Arogya Food and Beverages Products in Kulambi, Davangere, producing millet-based cookies under the brand Tapasvi.
He developed diverse millet cookies using millet blends, local milk, jaggery powder and selected natural sweeteners such as stevia.
whyChampion: Raghu shows how a home-based millet malt business started during COVID-19 can grow into a formal processing enterprise with machinery, branding and local employment — including women’s employment — while sourcing millets from FPOs.
achievement:
Secured a ₹30 lakh PMFME loan, established a millet-processing unit and developed millet-based cookies.
Became a mentor at IIM Bangalore and IIIT Bangalore and gained larger institutional orders. Trained at CFTRI, Mysuru (10-day programme on millet-based products).
successStory:
Started with home-based millet malt production during COVID-19 and developed it into a formal processing enterprise with machinery, branding, and employment.
Frequent power cuts once disrupted production; solar infrastructure now keeps the unit running, and the enterprise is expanding through institutional orders.
uniqueness: A rural millet value-addition model that links FPO-sourced millets to branded, ready-to-eat cookies for urban and institutional buyers — powered by solar to beat grid interruptions.
selcoEngagement: Solar infrastructure supported through the Millet Mentor programme and SELCO Foundation, addressing power interruptions in production.

name: Shoukatali Lambunavara
tagline: Solar-irrigated integrated farm on dry land
valueChainDetail: Crops & vegetables → local sales; poultry/eggs → village customers; fish → fish seller from Dharwad.
implementation: Farm ponds + rainwater harvesting + solar irrigation + automated drip & fertigation
profile: Shoukatali Lambunavara, 48, is a PhD graduate who owns and operates a 2-acre integrated farm involving agriculture, horticulture, forestry, poultry, dairy and fisheries in Nagnur village.
whyChampion: He demonstrates how rainwater harvesting, solar irrigation, organic practices and diversified farming can support productive farming without borewells or grid electricity on dry land. The farm has become a learning site for other farmers.
achievement:
Developed a diversified integrated farm with 30+ types of crops, poultry, dairy and fish farming. Other farmers visit the farm to learn about his practices.
Trained by KVK Dharwad, Krishi Kara Sangha, ATMA, the Fisheries Department, Agriculture & Horticulture Departments and Organic Farmers Associations.
successStory:
Barren land with failed borewells and ₹45,000/year in diesel irrigation costs has become a farm with 30+ crops, poultry and fish.
Irrigation changed from manual/diesel watering to automated solar drip irrigation — irrigation time fell from 7 hours to 2 hours per cycle, water wastage from 70% to below 10%. Average annual gross income rose from ~₹5 lakh to ₹7.11 lakh, with a reported net profit of ₹5.97 lakh.
uniqueness: A 100% solar-irrigated, zero-diesel, off-grid integrated farm on dry land — a live demonstration for rain-fed, water-scarce and off-grid farmers of how farm ponds and solar irrigation can sustain diversified farming.
selcoEngagement:
Introduced solar-powered irrigation to replace diesel pumping, and supported automated irrigation and fertigation.
Improved water-use efficiency through controlled irrigation, reduced labour, fuel costs and drudgery, and made the farm’s irrigation more energy-efficient and climate-resilient.

name: Bibi Jan Halemani
organisation: Convenor, Bibi Fatima Women’s SHG · CEO, Devadhanya FPO
valueChainDetail: Millet cultivation → collection → processing → value addition → branded products → marketing through Devadhanya FPO.
implementation: Solar power infrastructure for the millet processing unit (nominal EMI)
profile:
Bibi Jan Halemani is a college-educated farmer and millet entrepreneur from Teertha village, Dharwad. She is the Convenor of the Bibi Fatima Women’s SHG and CEO of Devadhanya FPO, working across millet cultivation, processing, value addition and marketing.
Products include ragi dosa mix, ragi multigrain atta, ragi malt, flours, vermicelli, biscuits, rotis and health drinks.
whyChampion: She promotes organic millet cultivation, indigenous seed conservation, collective processing and women-led livelihoods.
achievement:
Mobilised 1,000+ farmers and trains 25–30 farmers monthly. Established a community seed bank serving 22 villages and nearly 5,000 farmers, conserving around 300 seed varieties; supported formation of 52 SHGs.
Devadhanya FPO achieved ₹1.5 crore turnover. Received the UNDP Equator Initiative Award 2025 as the sole group awardee among 10 winners selected from 700+ applications across 103 countries.
successStory:
Through the Bibi Fatima Women’s SHG, farmers have come together to promote indigenous seeds and millet cultivation and create opportunities for processing and value addition.
After the solar intervention, the SHG’s electricity bill fell from about ₹8,000 to ₹3,000 per month, and reliable power keeps 9 processing units producing millet-based products for local and urban markets.
uniqueness: A women-led model combining a community seed bank (300 varieties, 31 seed producers), decentralised millet processing, solar-powered infrastructure and FPO-based marketing — improving women’s skills in processing and machinery operation.
selcoEngagement: SELCO Foundation provides solar power infrastructure for the millet processing unit on a nominal EMI basis, addressing high electricity costs and unreliable grid power — particularly during the rainy season — enabling reliable processing operations.

name: Boregowda
occupation: Farmer, seed conservator & organic farming leader
organisation: Founder, local organic farmers’ group · District Organic Farmers’ Collective
valueChainDetail: Indigenous / organic paddy (primary); ragi, sugarcane and millets (secondary). Covers transplanting, weeding, harvesting, threshing and drying, plus organic rice marketing and equipment rental.
implementation: Indigenous paddy conservation since 1997 · SELCO DRE-based mechanization
profile: Mr. Boregowda, popularly known as “Bhattada Boregowda”, 52, is a farmer, seed conservator and organic farming leader from Shivalli, Mandya. He conserves 500+ indigenous paddy varieties and promotes natural and organic farming.
whyChampion: He built his own paddy variety (Sidda Sanna), maintains a living repository of 500+ indigenous paddy varieties, has practised natural farming for decades, leads an organic farmers’ collective, and has inspired hundreds of farmers to move towards indigenous cultivars and sustainable farming.
achievement:
Conserved 500+ indigenous paddy varieties, established leadership in an organic farmers’ collective, and inspired hundreds of farmers to shift from hybrid/high-yielding varieties towards traditional cultivars.
The collective sells 500+ quintals of organic rice annually directly to customers.
successStory:
The site shows how indigenous paddy conservation can be combined with solar-powered mechanization. Labour fell from about 120 to 40 man-days per acre, production cost dropped ~30%, and yield loss reduced by ~20%.
Income increased from about ₹3.5–4 lakh to ₹4.5 lakh+ annually, solar-tool rentals earn ₹50,000+ per year, and women have re-engaged through lower-drudgery technologies.
uniqueness: A unique combination of 500+ indigenous paddy varieties, natural/organic farming, solar-powered mechanization, direct organic marketing, equipment rental and farmer learning — showing that traditional varieties can coexist with modern decentralised renewable energy.
selcoEngagement:
SELCO Foundation introduced DRE-based on-farm mechanization to address labour shortages, high costs, diesel dependence, soil degradation, climate vulnerability and drudgery.
Support included solar-powered paddy toolbar attachments, a mat-based transplanter, weeders, reapers and a thresher/dryer system.

name: Sunita Meti
occupation: Farmer – diversified agriculture, turmeric processing & mechanization services
valueChainDetail: Sugarcane, turmeric, groundnut, banana, guava and coconut — with turmeric processing (7–8 quintals) and mechanized farm services.
implementation: HALDAR MICRO TRAC – 750 battery-operated mini tractor with solar-assisted charging
profile:
Sunita Meti, 54 (PUC), owns and operates a 4-acre farm cultivating sugarcane, turmeric, groundnut, banana and guava, with 80 coconut trees, 2 buffaloes and 5 cows.
She operates a turmeric processing unit producing around 7–8 quintals of turmeric.
whyChampion: She demonstrates renewable-energy-based mechanization for small-scale farming — using a battery-operated mini tractor for her farm and providing tractor services to nearby farmers. She follows organic farming and uses solar energy and a gobar gas unit.
achievement: Recognised as a State-level Best Woman Entrepreneur Farmer. She performs farming operations independently, provides mechanization services to other farmers, and trains farmers through ATMA and Sanjeevini networks.
successStory:
Before: rented diesel tractors at ₹1,500/day and hired labour at ₹400/day, with costly delays in peak seasons.
After: her own battery-operated tractor with 7 factory implements and 2 custom-built tools. She saves around ₹70,000/year on labour and rentals, reduced labour dependency by ~100 days/year, and earns rental income at ~₹400/hour — a total yearly benefit of about ₹2.02 lakh.
uniqueness: Zero-emission, solar-charged mechanization sized for a small diversified farm, with user-led modifications (modified cultivator/bund former and a self-made blade leveller) — a role model for women in mechanized, sustainable farming.
selcoEngagement: SELCO Foundation introduced a renewable-energy-based battery-operated mini tractor to improve farm mechanization, reduce labour dependency, and support sustainable farming.

name: Hema Patil
valueChainDetail: Groundnut & safflower cultivation → decortication → oil extraction → filtering → bottling; oil cake → powdered feed; local markets & branded cold-pressed oil.
implementation: Solar-powered cold-press oil unit — 100 kg decorticator, oil extractor, cake breaker/powdering, filtering & bottling
profile: Mrs. Hema Patil, 50, is a farmer and agri-entrepreneur from Ron, Gadag, and a member of Somalingeshwara FPO. She maintains approximately 15 acres of agroforestry and a herd of around 100 sheep, alongside a solar-powered cold-press oil unit.
whyChampion: She has transformed her farming livelihood into a diversified agricultural enterprise by combining crop cultivation, agroforestry, livestock, oil processing, value addition and renewable energy — showing how decentralised renewable energy can support rural entrepreneurship and farm-level value addition.
achievement:
Established a farm-level cold-pressed oil processing enterprise, adopted solar-powered processing, introduced value addition of oil cake and developed local branding and bottling.
Her enterprise demonstrates the potential of rural women farmers to move beyond primary production into agro-processing.
successStory:
Hema transformed her traditional farming livelihood into a value-added oil processing enterprise. Processing groundnut and safflower with a solar cold-press system reduced energy dependence, eliminated manual and animal-based extraction, and created additional income from oil and oil-cake sales.
She saves approximately ₹3,000/month on electricity. Her son Hemanth actively operates and manages the unit.
uniqueness: Integration of farming, agroforestry, livestock and decentralised oil processing in one livelihood system — farm-grown oilseeds become branded cold-pressed oil, oil cake becomes feed, and two generations run the enterprise together.
selcoEngagement: SELCO Foundation introduced and supports the solar-powered cold-press oil processing intervention to address unreliable energy, drudgery, processing and value addition — including the decorticator, oil extractor, cake-processing, filtering and bottling units.

name: Syed Ghani Khan
occupation: Farmer, seed conservator, biodiversity campaigner & heritage curator
organisation: Sahaja Organics · Trainer, Janadhanya Vikasana · Member, Sahaja Samruddha
tagline: 1,350 paddy varieties & solar mini rice-mill hub
valueChainDetail: Paddy cultivation & milling; broken rice → flour/cookies; seed conservation → storage → poultry → livestock → organic inputs; direct marketing to consumers and organic networks.
implementation: 2023: Mini multi-stage rice mill & seed-bank deep freezer · 2024: Paddy Seed Diversity Hub, solar dryer, solar poultry coop & bio-fermenter
profile: Mr. Syed Ghani Khan, 50, is a farmer, seed conservator, biodiversity campaigner and heritage curator from Kirugavalu, Mandya. His field is a biodiversity hub with 1,350 indigenous paddy varieties, 120 varieties of mango and 100 varieties of ragi.
whyChampion: He is a Champion Farmer for his work in indigenous seed conservation, organic farming, biodiversity conservation, decentralised processing and renewable-energy adoption.
achievement:
Awards: District Arasamma Manase Gowda Krishi Prashasti, Krishi Pandita Prashasti, National Genome Saviour Award, National Innovation Saviour Award.
His integrated farm-based paddy value chain model combines seed conservation, cultivation, processing, value addition and direct marketing. The farm is a demonstration and learning site and provides milling services to 3–4 farmers per month.
successStory:
With SELCO Foundation’s DRE intervention, solar-powered processing reduced post-harvest losses from 10–20% to under 2% and diesel use from 200 litres/year to zero.
Annual gross income increased from ~₹4 lakh to ₹17.78 lakh and net profit from ~₹1.5 lakh to ₹13.52 lakh. Women’s labour dropped from 48 to under 6 workdays per season — around 90% less drudgery.
uniqueness: A single farm ecosystem uniting 1,350 paddy varieties, 120 mango and 100 ragi varieties, organic farming, decentralised paddy processing, value addition, livestock, poultry and renewable energy — traditional knowledge meeting modern DRE technology.
selcoEngagement: SELCO Foundation identified Syed Ghani Khan as a Champion Farmer and collaborated with him to establish a DRE-based Integrated Mini Paddy Value Chain Hub on his farm — solar thresher, power weeder, pre-cleaner, destoner, huller, separator, polisher, grader, pulveriser, bio-fermenter, solar poultry coop, DC refrigerator and solar dryer.
